metaDescription: Six small bathroom trash cans compared by size, lid style, motion sensor and soft close, from an open vanity basket to a waterproof sensor bin and 3-packs.
introParagraphs: A bathroom trash can has a different job from a kitchen bin. It holds tissues, cotton pads, floss and the occasional personal item, so it needs to be small, easy to wipe and discreet. It also has to live in a room that is damp, cramped and often shared, which rules out bulky bins and rewards ones with lids that close properly.

This lineup covers the main bathroom designs. The Rubbermaid vanity basket is a 1.5-gallon open-top bin, the Glad is a 1.2-gallon round stainless can with a step pedal and soft-close lid, and the Cesun is a 1.6-gallon slim steel can only 5.9 inches wide. The NETDOT has a pop-up button lid, the ELPHECO adds a motion sensor with IPX5 waterproofing, and the YGJT is a plastic three-pack that comes with bags.

We evaluated each bin on the listing specs and buyer feedback themes, thinking about the real bathroom problems: a lid that hides what is inside, a size that squeezes beside a toilet and a surface that resists splashes. Use this guide to find the one that matches your room rather than the one with the longest feature list.

products.name: Cesun 1.6 Gallon Slim Bathroom Trash Can with Soft Close Lid

specList.label: Dimensions
specList.value: 11.2 in H x 11.2 in L x 5.9 in W

products.description:
The Cesun is the most complete small bathroom can in this group. At 1.6 gallons it holds more than the 1.2-gallon Glad, and its slim rectangular body measures just 5.9 inches wide, so it slides into the gap between a toilet and a wall that rounder bins cannot use. The listing gives the full dimensions as 11.2 inches high and long, which helps you check the space before buying.

The lid is where it earns the top spot. A step pedal opens it hands-free, a soft-close mechanism lowers it silently, and a lid stay-open feature lets you leave it up while you tidy the room. A closed lid matters in a bathroom because it hides what is inside, and a silent close matters at night when someone is asleep nearby.

The matte black metal is described as anti-rust and anti-fingerprint, a useful pairing in a damp room where chrome spots easily. Compared with the Glad, it holds more and is slimmer, and compared with the plastic three-packs, it feels more permanent. It does cost more per can than the multipacks, and it needs a small liner that fits its narrow shape.
products.bestFor: Tight bathrooms that need a quiet, closed-lid can.
pros: Slim 5.9-inch body fits beside a toilet
Step pedal keeps hands off the lid

products.name: Glad 1.2 Gallon Round Stainless Steel Step Trash Can
products.description:
The Glad is the smallest bin here, and that is both its charm and its limit. A 1.2-gallon capacity fits rooms with very little space, such as a powder room, an office corner or a bedside, and the round shape tucks easily into a corner. The brushed stainless steel finish is meant to blend with most decor.

A foot pedal opens the lid for hands-free use, and the soft-close lid keeps trash out of sight while avoiding a slam. The listing positions it for small rooms, which is where a larger step can would feel oversized. For a single person who generates only a few tissues and cotton pads a day, the volume is plenty.

For a family bathroom the size can be limiting, since a small bag fills quickly and you must empty it often. It also gives up the flat-backed shape of the Cesun, so it wastes a little more wall space. Compared with the plastic three-packs, it is sturdier and more refined, and compared with the ELPHECO, it has no batteries to maintain. If you want a tidy steel can for a small powder room, it is a good fit.
products.bestFor: Powder rooms and single-person bathrooms with limited space.
pros: Compact round body fits in corners
Foot pedal avoids touching the lid
cons: Fills quickly in a family bathroom
Round shape wastes some wall space

products.name: ELPHECO 2 Gallon Motion Sensor Bathroom Trash Can

specList.label: Dimensions
specList.value: 10 in L x 5.3 in W x 11.42 in H

products.description:
The ELPHECO is the one to consider if you want a bathroom can that you never touch. A motion sensor opens the lid when a hand passes over it, and the listing says the sensing reduces unnecessary openings to extend battery life. If you keep your hand over the sensor, the lid stays open, which is helpful when you are clearing the counter.

IPX5 waterproofing is a thoughtful addition for a bathroom, because splashes from a sink, a mopped floor or a shower should not harm the electronics. The body is ABS plastic in a white gold finish, and the listing gives its size as 10 inches long, 5.3 inches wide and 11.42 inches tall, so it is slim enough to fit in a narrow space. Capacity is 2 gallons, larger than the Cesun.

The listing makes clear that the customer must install 2 AA batteries and follow set-up steps, so there is some assembly and ongoing upkeep. That makes it less carefree than the Glad or Cesun. If you value a hygienic, hands-free can for a shared bathroom or guest bath, and you do not mind swapping batteries, it is the most convenient design here.
products.bestFor: Shared or guest bathrooms where a hands-free lid matters.
pros: IPX5 waterproof rating for damp rooms
Two gallons holds more than most here
Lid stays open while a hand is over it
cons: More parts to fail than a pedal can
White gold finish may not suit every bathroom

products.name: N. NETDOT 2.6 Gallon Pop-Up Lid Trash Can 3-Pack
products.description:
The NETDOT three-pack is a clever answer to a household that needs several bathroom bins. Each can holds 10 liters, listed as 2.6 gallons, and has a slim rectangular body that the listing says stores inside cabinets, underneath counters and in other small spaces. Three cans let you cover the main bathroom, a guest bath and a bedroom without buying separately.

The pop-up lid is operated by a tap on a button. The press top opens and closes at a touch, so you do not need a pedal or a hand lift. This works well in a bathroom where floor space is tight and a pedal would be hard to reach, and the closed lid hides contents between uses.

Because it is a plastic multipack, it is lighter and plainer than the Cesun or Glad. The listing does not claim soft close or a stay-open feature. Compared with the YGJT three-pack, you get a lid rather than an open top, and a larger capacity at 2.6 gallons against 1.8 gallons. For a home that needs many covered bins at an easy price level, it is a practical pick.
products.bestFor: Homes that want several lidded bins for different rooms.
pros: Pop-up lid opens with a tap
cons: Button must be pressed by hand

products.name: Rubbermaid 1.5 Gallon Vanity Wastebasket
products.description:
The Rubbermaid is the plain, honest choice. It is a 1.5-gallon open basket with a reinforced rim that the listing says holds up to daily use, and a smooth inner surface that makes mess cleanup easy. There is no lid, no pedal and no battery, which means nothing can fail.

Its size is sized for under a sink, a vanity or an office desk. Because it is open at the top, you can drop items in quickly, and you can see when it needs emptying. It suits households where hiding the contents is not a priority, or where a lid is rarely needed.

The tradeoff is clear. Without a lid, odors and sights are not contained, and a pet or a child can reach in. Compared with the Cesun or Glad, it is far simpler and has no hygiene advantage from a closed top. Compared with the YGJT three-pack, it is a single sturdy basket from a well-known brand. If you want a no-fuss bin for a bathroom where discretion is not a concern, this is the one.
products.bestFor: Bathrooms where a simple open basket is enough.
cons: No lid to hide contents or odor
Pets and children can reach in

products.name: YGJT 1.8 Gallon Round Trash Can 3-Pack with Bags
products.description:
The YGJT is a set of three round plastic wastebaskets with bags in the box. Each can holds 1.8 gallons, a sensible size for next to a toilet, under a cabinet or beside a sink. The listing says the plastic will not chip, dent or fade even after long use, which is a practical claim in a damp room.

The included bags are the quiet advantage. Small liners can be harder to find than standard kitchen bags, so having a starter supply saves a trip. The round, slim shape fits tight corners and is easy to carry to the sink for a rinse when the inside needs cleaning.

It has no lid, so contents and odors are visible and not contained, a drawback against the NETDOT pop-up and the Cesun. It also offers no sensor or soft close. Compared with the Rubbermaid, you get three cans and bags, but less brand pedigree. If you need several simple open bins and want bags to start, the YGJT makes sense.
products.bestFor: Households that want multiple open bins with bags included.
cons: Open top shows contents and odors

buyingCriteria.explanation: Bathroom space is tight, so measure the gap beside the toilet or under the sink before you buy. The Cesun is only 5.9 inches wide, the ELPHECO is 5.3 inches wide, and the round Glad suits corners. A bin that is too wide will block a door or catch your leg. Remember that taller bins need clearance too, especially under shelves, and that a pedal needs a bit of floor space in front of it so your foot can reach. Write the measurements down before you shop and compare them with the dimensions in each listing.

A lid hides contents and contains odor, while an open top is quicker and simpler. The Cesun, Glad, ELPHECO and NETDOT all have lids, and the Rubbermaid and YGJT do not. In a shared or guest bathroom, a closed lid is usually worth having. In a private bathroom, an open basket can be perfectly fine.

Bathroom bins open by foot pedal, press button, motion sensor or simply by being open. The Cesun and Glad use pedals, the NETDOT uses a pop-up press top, and the ELPHECO uses a sensor. A pedal needs floor room, a button needs a free hand, and a sensor needs batteries. Pick the style that fits how your bathroom is arranged.

Bathrooms are damp, so materials matter. The ELPHECO carries an IPX5 waterproof rating, the Cesun is described as anti-rust, and the plastic YGJT is said not to chip, dent or fade. Steel without a good finish can rust over time. Choose a finish that stands up to steam and splashes.

Bathroom bins range from 1.2 gallons on the Glad to 2.6 gallons on the NETDOT. A tiny can fills fast and needs frequent emptying. Small bags can be harder to source, so a pack with bags, like the YGJT, is convenient. Match the capacity to household size.

A bathroom is often next to a bedroom, so a loud lid is a nuisance. The Cesun and Glad list soft-close lids, while the Rubbermaid and YGJT have no lid at all to bang. A sensor like the ELPHECO is also quiet. Consider who sleeps nearby. A pedal can that stands on a tile floor also transmits a tap, so a rubber foot or a rug beneath the Glad or Cesun cuts the sound further.

faq.q: What size trash can is best for a bathroom?
faq.a: Most bathroom cans hold between about one and three gallons. The Glad at 1.2 gallons suits one person, while the NETDOT at 2.6 gallons suits a family. Measure the space, and think about how often you want to empty it. A single person can happily use the smaller cans, while a family sharing one bathroom will want the extra capacity to avoid daily trips.

faq.q: Do I need a lid on a bathroom trash can?
faq.a: A lid hides contents and helps with odor, which matters in shared bathrooms. The Cesun, Glad, NETDOT and ELPHECO all have lids. In a private bathroom, an open basket like the Rubbermaid may be enough.

faq.q: Are motion sensor bathroom cans reliable?
faq.a: They work well when the batteries are fresh and the sensor is clean. The ELPHECO uses 2 AA batteries and an IPX5 waterproof rating, but it still needs occasional upkeep. If you want zero maintenance, a pedal can is simpler.

faq.q: How do I stop bathroom bins from smelling?
faq.a: Use a lidded can, empty it often and rinse the inside when something spills. Open baskets need more frequent emptying. Humidity can make smells worse, so keep the room ventilated. Tossing used tissues into a small bag that you knot before dropping into the bin also keeps the can itself fresher between rinses.

faq.q: Where do I find liners for tiny cans?
faq.a: Small liners are sold in packs for bathroom bins, though sizes vary. The YGJT three-pack comes with bags, which helps. Check the capacity of your can before buying. If your bin has an unusual narrow shape, such as the Cesun, test one liner first, since a bag that bunches at the sides makes the lid sit crooked.

faq.q: Will steel rust in a bathroom?
faq.a: It can if the finish is poor. The Cesun is described as anti-rust and the Glad uses brushed stainless steel. Wipe off standing water and avoid harsh cleaners.
If you need bins in several rooms, yes. The NETDOT offers three lidded cans and the YGJT three open cans with bags. For one bathroom, a single quality can like the Cesun may serve you better.
